accessory_occlusion_safety.compiled_prompt_en: EYEWEAR OCCLUSION SAFETY: If sunglasses, dark glasses, goggles, or tinted lenses appear, treat the lenses as a coherent physical surface. For opaque or mirrored lenses, hide both eyes fully and naturally behind the lenses; do not render visible pupils, irises, eyelashes, or a second pair of eyes through dark glass. For translucent tinted lenses, keep any implied eyes soft, low-contrast, anatomically aligned, and subordinate to lens tint and reflection; never create sharp floating pupils or mismatched gaze through the lenses. When identity fidelity matters more than the accessory, remove the sunglasses or place them lifted above the eyes or held in one hand. Keep the frame aligned to the nose bridge, temples, and facial plane.

modes.rule_en: Keep both eyes naturally visible and aligned.
Hide both eyes fully behind coherent dark or mirrored lenses. No through-lens pupils, irises, eyelashes, or duplicate eyes.
Allow only soft low-contrast anatomically aligned eye hints beneath the tint. Lens surface and reflection remain dominant.
Place sunglasses above the eyes or held in one hand when recognizable eye identity is important.
Keep both eyes readable, aligned, and naturally visible through transparent lenses. Allow only restrained physically plausible glints or small reflections.

forbidden_patterns: sharp visible pupils through opaque lenses
lens frame detached from nose bridge
one eye visible and one eye unrealistically erased unless physically occluded
large white reflection blobs hiding both pupils without a plausible flash angle
duplicated or warped eyes behind clear lenses
floating glasses frame detached from nose bridge or temples
lens reflections inconsistent with camera-flash position
accessory_occlusion_safety.clear_lens_flash_prompt_en: CLEAR-LENS EYEWEAR SAFETY: When clear prescription glasses appear, keep both eyes anatomically aligned, readable, and naturally visible through transparent lenses. Treat each lens as one coherent optical surface attached to a stable frame resting on the nose bridge and temples. Under direct camera flash, allow only restrained physically plausible edge glints or small source reflections; do not place large white reflection blobs across both pupils unless the camera-source geometry genuinely supports it. Avoid duplicated irises, warped eyes, asymmetrical magnification, floating frames, detached temples, opaque clear lenses, and reflections that ignore the flash position. If the eyes become unreadable, reduce the reflection rather than inventing through-lens anatomy.

lighting_physics_grammar.principle: Light physics and composition perspective are resolved together: source direction, shadow projection, foreground plane, scene geometry, and subject angle must agree.
lighting_physics_grammar.compiled_prompt_en: LIGHTING PHYSICS SAFETY: Build the scene from a small number of physically plausible emitters. Keep one dominant key-light logic and make highlight, shadow, catchlight, rim light, reflected color, and cast-shadow direction agree with the source geometry. Do not place bright rims on surfaces that cannot see the source. Do not light both sides of the face equally when using one directional key. Respect window-edge penumbra, indoor falloff, outdoor atmospheric fill, railing and hand occlusion shadows, and color spill only on surfaces facing the spill. Preserve skin detail and avoid clipping forehead, nose bridge, cheek, shoulder, white clothing, and reflective jewelry. Keep practical lamps, sun beams, neon reflections, haze, and ambient fill subordinate to a coherent exposure hierarchy. Avoid impossible multi-directional highlights, disconnected shadows, random color patches, floating catchlights, duplicated cast shadows, and overexposed facial planes. HARD-SHADOW AND DIRECT-FLASH EXTENSION: For hard window sun, blind shadows, leaf shadows, hand shadows, and architectural occluders, preserve one continuous source path: shadow bands must keep a consistent direction, scale, softness, and surface continuity as they cross wall, clothing, hand, face, and furniture. Do not create decorative stripe patterns that change direction or float independently across the face. For direct on-camera flash, respect near-lens source geometry, inverse-square falloff, hard short cast shadows behind nearby objects, bright foreground priority, darker ambient background, and restrained specular response on skin, glasses, tableware, and glossy surfaces. Do not combine direct-flash flattening with unrelated cinematic rim lights unless a second visible practical source explains them. OCCLUDED-BEAM AND TWILIGHT-FLASH EXTENSION: For narrow warm beams, slit light, projector-like pools, door-gap light, and foreground veils, preserve one explainable aperture or occluder path. The lit region, shadow edge, penumbra, falloff, and surface continuity must agree across hair, eyelids, nose bridge, lips, neck, clothing, bedding, wall, and nearby objects. Keep facial landmarks readable even when much of the frame remains dark. For dusk beach direct flash, keep the near-lens flash responsible for foreground face and skin exposure while the sunset sky remains a separate low ambient field; do not brighten the ocean, sand, and distant horizon as if they share the same flash distance. For rooftop blue-hour portraits, allow one rear-side warm sunset rim and one restrained front fill or near-camera flash only when their roles remain visibly separable. Avoid blown halos, duplicated suns, arbitrary orange patches, flat beauty fill that erases twilight depth, and shadow bands that float independently of an occluder. WIND, FLARE, MOTION-BLUR, AND BEDROOM-LIFESTYLE EXTENSION: For wind-led close-ups, keep hair strands attached to one airflow vector and allow only explainable strand shadows across skin. Preserve at least one clear eye, the nose bridge, and the mouth contour as identity anchors. For hand-intercepted warm beams, keep the hand, beam edge, face patch, and cast shadow on one aperture path. For golden-hour backlight, align lens flare, bloom, warm rim, and highlight roll-off to one low-sun axis; do not paste random colored orbs across the frame. For slow-shutter and panning portraits, separate subject motion, camera movement, background streak direction, and crisp post-layout typography. Retain one readable identity anchor and anatomically continuous limbs. For bedroom lifestyle scenes, use one window direction with plausible wall, desk, textile, and prop bounce; avoid overexposed skin, cluttered facial zones, floating headphones, and generic showroom rooms. SEASONAL-FLORAL-TRANSIT EXTENSION: Keep scarf volume separate from face, forest light subordinate to canopy depth, autumn leaves subordinate to gravity and depth, mixed vehicle practicals separate from skin exposure, flower stems physically attached, transit corridor perspective coherent, and glass reflections offset from the physical subject. Resolve camera and projection hierarchy alongside light direction. Hard shadows, reflections, practicals, foreground blur, and architecture must belong to traceable planes.
universal_rules: Every lighting preset must define a dominant source and one exposure priority.
Mixed color temperatures require a clear spatial boundary or believable reflected spill.
Hard sunlight requires directional cast shadows and non-uniform facial illumination.
Window light must respect window position, wall orientation, and edge penumbra.
Neon light is usually reflected or signage spill, not uniform face paint.
Railing, hands, cups, and foreground objects cast occlusion shadows only when they block the source path.
Catchlights must be few, aligned, and explainable by visible or implied emitters.
White clothing, satin, pearls, wet skin, and glossy surfaces require highlight roll-off control.
Structured hard-shadow patterns must remain continuous across connected surfaces and follow one occluder geometry.
Direct on-camera flash must preserve near-lens source geometry, hard short shadows, foreground priority, and darker ambient background.
Clear prescription lenses remain transparent; flash reflections must be restrained and camera-position-consistent.
Narrow warm beams and spot pools must follow one aperture or occluder path with coherent penumbra and falloff.
Dusk direct flash must expose the near subject without flattening the distant sky, sea, or horizon into the same light field.
Blue-hour rim-fill scenes may combine rear-side sunset rim and restrained front fill only when the two emitter roles remain separable.
Foreground haze, door gaps, glass reflections, and veils must behave as depth-bearing optical layers rather than decorative overlays.
Wind-led hair must follow one dominant airflow vector and preserve readable recognition anchors.
A hand entering an occluded beam must cast source-consistent shadows on the face and nearby surfaces.
Golden-hour lens flare must align with one low-sun lens axis and remain subordinate to identity readability.
Intentional motion blur must separate camera panning, subject motion, background streaks, and crisp post-layout typography.
Bedroom lifestyle light must respect the visible or implied window direction and local textile or wall bounce.

composition_perspective_grammar.principle: Composition is not decoration. Resolve camera position, projection family, horizon, vanishing logic, subject plane, foreground plane, background plane, light projection, and typography plane before style embellishment.
composition_perspective_grammar.compiled_prompt_en: Resolve the camera and plane hierarchy before styling: camera height, lens behavior, horizon, vanishing point logic, subject plane, foreground occlusion plane, background geometry, light projection plane, and typography-safe post-layout zone. Preserve one coherent optical hierarchy and reject warped architecture, pasted foregrounds, detached props, arbitrary shadow direction, impossible foreshortening, and text crossing recognition landmarks.
universal_rules: Camera position precedes styling.
Foreground occlusion must belong to a real near plane.
Architecture, railings, vehicles, corridors, tables, steps, and horizons must keep one perspective logic.
Hard shadows require a traceable projection path.
Typography is a separate post-layout plane and must remain crisp outside facial landmarks.
Foreshortening is allowed only when limb continuity remains anatomically readable.
